source_screen.scope_of_source: The source studies n-complete bayonet codes (cbc): n-element X in a^[n] b a^[n] with {a^n} union X a code. Its theorems are about cbc, borders, Hajos factorizations and the strong triangle conjecture (Thm6.5: true when n is a cbc Hajos number). It does not claim Shor's code has or lacks a finite completion; Cordero writes that a code violating the triangle inequalities inside a finite maximal code would refute the factorization conjecture.

new_C_specific_written_consequence.statement: Let M be any finite UD factor-complete binary code (equivalently, a finite maximal code) containing all16 literal Shor words, and let a^n be its unique pure-a word. (A) Under the classical named imports RSS89 (as quoted by Cordero Thm1.1) and Tijdeman's multiplier theorem, 660=2^2*3*5*11 divides n. (B) Under the additional Cordero arXiv-v1 imports Prop2.6, Prop3.3 and Thm7.2, 1320=2^3*3*5*11 divides n.
new_C_specific_written_consequence.step0_elementary: If two distinct Shor words a^i b a^j and a^i' b a^j' had i=i' and j=j' mod n, the word a^max(i,i') b a^max(j,j') would have two factorizations padded by powers of a^n, so M would not be UD. Hence the16 reductions mod n are distinct. C_M(b) has exactly n elements by the named import Cordero Thm1.4 (BPR Prop12.2.4/Thm2.5.13), so n>=16. Every Shor exponent is at most14<n, so C is contained literally in X:=C_M(b).
new_C_specific_written_consequence.A_RSS_Tijdeman_proof: b is in M. By RSS89, P={k: a^k b^m in M for some m>=1} and Q={k: b^m a^k in M for some m>=1} form a direct factorization P+Q=Z_n, |P||Q|=n. The Shor words give {0,3,8,11} in P and {0,1,7,13,14} in Q. Tijdeman: if gcd(t,|P|)=1 then tP+Q=Z_n is again direct, and symmetrically for Q. Hand checks, each giving two distinct representations of one residue: t=2 on P: 0+7=6+1, so 2 divides |P|. t=3 on Q: 0+3=3+0 (3=3*1 in 3Q), so 3 divides |Q|. t=5 on Q: 3+5=8+0, so 5 divides |Q|. t=11 on Q: 0+11=11+0, so 11 divides |Q|. t=8 on Q: 0+8=8+0, so |Q| is even. Hence 2*(2*3*5*11)=660 divides n.
new_C_specific_written_consequence.B_Cordero_multiplier_proof: X lies in the stable set C_M of Prop2.6, so {X} is compatible. By Prop3.3, C_M is bordered by a size-n factorization (P',Q'), |P'||Q'|=n. By Thm7.2 with E=C_M, phi_{d1,d2}(X)={a^(d1 i mod n) b a^(d2 j mod n)} is an n-cbc, so {a^n} union phi_{d1,d2}(X) is UD, whenever gcd(d1,|Q'|)=gcd(d2,|P'|)=1. Literal relations among images of Shor words exclude coprimality. d2=2: (a^3ba^8)(b)=(a^3b)(a^8b), with a^3ba^8 the image of a^3ba^4. d2=3: (ba^3)(b)=(b)(a^3b). d2=5: (ba^5)(a^3b)=(b)(a^8b). d2=11: (ba^11)(b)=(b)(a^11b). d1=2: (ba^7)(b)=(ba)(a^6b), with a^6b the image of a^3b. So 2,3,5,11 divide |P'| and 2 divides |Q'|, giving 4|n. If 8 did not divide n, write n=4m with m odd and take d2=m+2. It is odd, and d2=2 mod each odd prime of |P'|, since those primes divide m. So gcd(d2,|P'|)=1, but 4*d2=n+8 maps a^3ba^4 to a^3ba^8 and repeats the d2=2 relation. Contradiction. Hence 8|n and 1320|n.
new_C_specific_written_consequence.consistency_check: 1320 is not a cbc Hajos number. This agrees with the separate named-import route: C_M(b) violates the triangle property at k=15 (16 words of length<=15), so Cordero Thm6.5 (proof unread) forbids a cbc-Hajos n.
new_C_specific_written_consequence.how_checked: Every displayed relation is a literal identity between two products of two words, checked by hand by comparing a-exponents. The residue choice d2=m+2 is checked by hand. No program, eval, enumeration or replay was used.
new_C_specific_written_consequence.nonclaims: This is a NECESSARY condition on the a-order of any completion. It is not a completion, not a nonexistence proof, and not the requested blocking invariant on every PR-saturated prefix. The method leaves every n in 1320Z open. It uses no commutative-equivalence, factorization or triangle conjecture. No novelty is claimed: Cordero Example7.3 applies the same multiplier method to another code, and Cor19a/Cor19b (unread) may already state Shor-specific order constraints. The Tijdeman and RSS statements are recalled or quoted, not reconstructed.
